evals.name: flagrant-violations
evals.prompt: Review the skill at ~/.claude/skills/reviewing-skills-workspace/fixtures/claude-pdf-helper against Anthropic's best practices and tell me what's wrong and how to fix it.
evals.expected_output: Catches the blocking issues (reserved word 'claude' in name; first-person, when-less description) and the major ones (nested references advanced.md->details.md, punting analyze.py, voodoo constants 47/5, verbose PDF explainer, too many library options, Windows path, time-sensitive note). Verdict is not-compliant/needs-work with prioritized fixes.

evals.name: subtle-quality-issues
evals.prompt: Can you check my converting-images skill? It's at ~/.claude/skills/reviewing-skills-workspace/fixtures/converting-images. Frontmatter's fine I think, just want a quality pass.
evals.expected_output: Passes the mechanical/frontmatter checks but surfaces the judgment issues: menu of 5 libraries instead of one default, verbose raster-vs-vector background that Claude already knows, magic constants Q=87/R=3 in convert.py, no concrete examples. Does not fabricate frontmatter failures.

evals.name: clean-skill-no-overreach
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this is a well-written skill: passes it with a positive verdict, at most noting a minor gap like absence of evals. Critically, does NOT invent problems to look thorough.
